title: Nebuchadnezzar II becomes King of Babylon
fact: Nebuchadnezzar II, more correctly spelled Nebuchadrezzar II, meaning "Nabu, watch over my heir", was the second king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, ruling from the death of his father Nabopolassar in 605 BC to his own death in 562 BC.

title: Hammurabi becomes King of Babylon
fact: Hammurabi, also spelled Hammurapi, was the sixth Amorite king of the Old Babylonian Empire, reigning from c. 1792 to c.

title: Ashurbanipal becomes King of Babylon
fact: Ashurbanipal was the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 669 BC to his death in 631.

title: Sennacherib becomes King of Babylon
fact: Sennacherib was the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 705 BC until his assassination in 681 BC.

title: Sargon II becomes King of Babylon
fact: Sargon II was the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 722 BC to his death in battle in 705.

title: Nabonidus becomes King of Babylon
fact: Nabonidus was the last king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, ruling from 556 BC to the fall of Babylon to the Achaemenian Empire under Cyrus the Great in 539 BC.

title: Tiglath-Pileser III becomes King of Babylon
fact: Tiglath-Pileser III was the Neo-Assyrian emperor from 745 BC to his death in 727.

title: Shalmaneser V becomes King of Babylon
fact: Shalmaneser V was the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 727 BC to his deposition and death in 722 BC.

title: Shamshi-Adad V becomes King of Babylon
fact: Shamshi-Adad V was the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 824 to 811 BC.

title: Shamash-shum-ukin becomes King of Babylon
fact: Šamaš-šuma-ukin, was king of Babylon as a vassal of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 668 BC to his death in 648.

title: Samsu-iluna becomes King of Babylon
fact: Samsu-iluna was the seventh king of the founding Amorite dynasty of Babylon.

title: Marduk-apla-iddina II becomes King of Babylon
fact: Marduk-apla-iddina II was a Chaldean ruler from the Bit-Yakin tribe, originally established in the territory that once made the Sealand in southern Babylonia.
